bills.title: Generative AI Training Data Transparency Disclosure
bills.summary: Requires generative AI developers to publicly disclose training dataset information. A federal judge denied xAI's preliminary injunction motion to block enforcement, finding the law likely does not violate the First Amendment. Applying the Central Hudson test, the court held the state's interest in factual transparency was substantial and the disclosure requirements not more extensive than necessary.
bills.status_detail: Constitutionally upheld — federal court denied preliminary injunction motion by xAI; law effective January 2026

bills.title: AI Health Care Decision-Making Restrictions
bills.summary: An Illinois HB 1806-style bill that would restrict AI use in health care decision-making. Passed out of committee.
bills.status_detail: Passed committee

bills.title: Automated Decision Systems in Employment Disclosure and Audit Requirements
bills.summary: Would require disclosures to applicants and employees when automated decision systems (ADS) are used in employment, mandate human review for final employment decisions, and require annual independent bias audits. Employers would be required to provide individuals with access to relevant data, opportunities to correct errors, and the ability to appeal adverse decisions. Clarifies that discriminatory outcomes from automated systems may constitute violations of state anti-discrimination law.
bills.status_detail: Referred to Joint Committee on Labor and Public Employees
sponsors: Joint Committee on Labor and Public Employees

bills.title: Chatbot and AI Agent Disclosure Requirements
bills.summary: Would require businesses to clearly disclose when consumers are interacting with a chatbot, AI agent, or avatar during commercial transactions. Includes a private right of action. References AI agents alongside chatbots and avatars — one of the first instances of the term appearing directly in legislation. Passed through committee after introduction.
bills.status_detail: Introduced and passed committee this week

bills.title: Conversational AI Services Disclosure and Minor Protections
bills.summary: Would require operators of 'conversational AI services' to provide nonhuman disclosures to minors every three hours and restrict engagement optimization. Would require age verification before allowing access to a chatbot that could provide sexually explicit synthetic content. Operators would be required to offer parental management tools and be prohibited from causing or programming a chatbot designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care.
bills.status_detail: Passed first chamber

bills.title: AI Companion Chatbot Safeguards for Minors
bills.summary: Requires certain safeguards for minors using AI companion chatbots. Amended to add definitions such as crisis intervention and emotional dependency. Passed first chamber.
bills.status_detail: Passed first chamber; amended to add definitions for crisis intervention and emotional dependency

bills.title: Prohibition on Data-Driven Pricing in Food Sales
bills.summary: Prohibits data-driven pricing in food sales. Amended to remove specific references to loyalty programs, specify each violation is a separate cause of action, and define 'personally identifiable information.' Passed first chamber.
bills.status_detail: Passed first chamber; amended to remove loyalty program references and add PII definition

bills.title: Chatbot Mental Health Safety Protocols
bills.summary: Mandates chatbot mental health protocols. Amended to extend disclosure requirements to every three hours (previously every hour), limit safety protocols to suicidal ideation, and add data privacy protections. Passed first chamber.
bills.status_detail: Passed first chamber; amended to extend disclosure interval to 3 hours and narrow safety protocols to suicidal ideation

bills.title: Youth Online Safety and AI Companion Chatbot Regulations
bills.summary: This bill has been amended and no longer includes provisions regulating AI companion chatbots, now focusing solely on youth online safety requirements for social media platforms.
bills.status_detail: Amended to remove AI companion chatbot provisions; now focuses on youth online safety for social media only

bills.title: Prohibition on Surveillance-Based Data in Individualized Pricing and Wage Decisions
bills.summary: Would prohibit the use of surveillance-based data to inform individualized pricing or wage decisions through automated decision systems. Exceptions would allow differential pricing or wages when justified by actual cost differences, part of transparent and broadly available discount programs, or (for insurers) based solely on risk-relevant data.
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: Prohibition on Surveillance-Based Data in Individualized Pricing and Wage Decisions (Senate Companion)
bills.summary: Companion bill to HF 4131. Would prohibit the use of surveillance-based data to inform individualized pricing or wage decisions through automated decision systems. Exceptions would allow differential pricing or wages when justified by actual cost differences, part of transparent and broadly available discount programs, or (for insurers) based solely on risk-relevant data.
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: Artificial Intelligence Definition
bills.summary: Signed by Governor Reeves (R). Adds a definition of 'artificial intelligence' to Mississippi code, largely modeled on the OECD's AI definition.
bills.status_detail: Signed by Governor Reeves (R)

bills.title: Right to Compute
bills.summary: Would establish a right to compute, similar to enacted Montana SB 212. Passed committee.
bills.status_detail: Passed committee

bills.title: Prohibition on AI Delivery of Licensed Professional Services
bills.summary: Would prohibit the use of AI to deliver any service that requires a professional license unless the service is provided by a licensed practitioner. Passed committee.
bills.status_detail: Passed committee

bills.title: Prohibition on AI-Powered Chatbot Toys for Young Children
bills.summary: Would prohibit the manufacture and sale of AI-powered chatbot toys for children under thirteen in New York for five years. Would also mandate a comprehensive interagency study on the risks and benefits of chatbot toys to child users, including data collection and retention practices. Follows California's SB 867 and Maryland's HB 1261 on similar themes.
bills.status_detail: Introduced

bills.title: Generative AI Inaccuracy Disclosure Notice Requirement
bills.summary: Would require operators of GenAI systems to display a notice on the system's interface that GenAI outputs may be inaccurate. Failure to provide the notice would result in a civil penalty up to $1,000 per violation. Passed both chambers.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers

bills.title: AI Companion Chatbot Safety and Disclosure Framework
bills.summary: Passed the legislature; awaiting Governor's signature (5 business days). Establishes a companion chatbot framework similar to California's SB 243. Defines 'artificial intelligence companion' as a system designed to simulate a sustained human-like relationship through personalized interactions and ongoing dialogue about personal or emotional topics (excludes customer service, education, financial services, healthcare, business productivity, and technical assistance uses). Would require clear and conspicuous disclosures, mandated safety protocols including crisis resource referrals, additional protections for minors against emotional dependence or romantic simulation, and prohibitions against engagement-maximization directed at minors. Includes a private right of action.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; sent to Governor (5 business days for signature)

bills.title: Coercive Suicide Definition and AI System Liability
bills.summary: Would define the term 'coercive suicide' (advising or encouraging another person to attempt to commit suicide) and previously would have clarified when an entity owning an AI system would commit this offense. The bill passed through its first chamber but was amended to remove all references to AI systems.
bills.status_detail: Passed first chamber; amended to remove all AI system provisions

bills.title: AI Companion Chatbot Safety Requirements
bills.summary: Amended in committee to require a study on the potential regulation of AI systems and generative AI chatbots in Tennessee. Previously would have set a series of safety and disclosure requirements for companion chatbots.
bills.status_detail: Amended in committee to require study on AI regulation; passed committee

bills.title: Healthcare Scope of Practice Expansion Including Technological Innovations
bills.summary: Would establish a process within the state licensure board for medical professionals for expanding healthcare practitioners' scope of practice that includes technological innovations such as AI. Passed both chambers; sent to Governor.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; sent to Governor

bills.title: Large Online Platform Provenance Data Detection and Disclosure
bills.summary: Would require large online platforms (over 2 million monthly users) to detect, disclose, and preserve provenance data and provide user tools to inspect that information. Passed both chambers; sent to Governor.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; sent to Governor

bills.title: Utah Data Privacy Law Updates for Automated Decision-Making
bills.summary: Would update Utah's data privacy laws by introducing new definitions for automated decision-making and profiling, including requiring the development of a data privacy framework that incorporates best practices for automated decision-making. Passed both chambers; sent to Governor.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; sent to Governor

bills.title: AI Chatbot Regulation
bills.summary: A chatbot bill that failed to advance before the end of Utah's legislative session.
bills.status_detail: Failed to advance before end of Utah's legislative session

bills.title: AI Chatbot and Frontier Model Regulation
bills.summary: A chatbot bill that also addressed frontier models. Failed to advance before the end of Utah's legislative session. The outcome came amid reported federal attention urging Utah lawmakers to reconsider the proposal, reflecting broader tensions over state-level AI regulation and federal engagement.
bills.status_detail: Failed to advance before end of Utah's legislative session amid reported federal pressure on lawmakers

bills.title: Education AI Regulatory Sandbox Program
bills.summary: Would have established an education AI regulatory sandbox program. Failed to advance before the end of Utah's legislative session.
bills.status_detail: Failed to advance before end of Utah's legislative session

bills.title: AI Health Communications Disclaimer and Mental Health Chatbot Restrictions
bills.summary: Would mandate disclaimers for AI-generated patient communications, restrict advertising and data collection for mental health chatbots, and enumerate a list of 'neurological rights'. Passed committee; heads to the Appropriations Committee.
bills.status_detail: Passed committee; referred to Appropriations Committee

bills.title: Independent AI Verification Organizations Study
bills.summary: As amended, directs the Joint Commission on Technology and Science (JCOTS) to study the feasibility and impact of establishing a framework for independent verification organizations (IVOs) that would assess whether AI systems adhere to safety standards aimed at preventing personal injury or property damage. Prior to amendments, the bill would have directly created a licensing framework for IVOs.
bills.status_detail: Amended on floor to require JCOTS study instead of direct IVO licensing framework; passed both chambers

bills.title: GenAI Provenance Data and Government AI Disclosure Requirements
bills.summary: Amended in committee before passage. Would require covered providers to include provenance data in any content created or materially altered by their GenAI system, with exclusions for video games. Would also require government agencies that make AI systems available to consumers to disclose that consumers are interacting with an AI system, including provenance data. Passed both chambers.
bills.status_detail: Amended in committee; passed both chambers

bills.title: AI Companion Chatbot Safeguards and Minor Protections
bills.summary: Would require operators of AI companion chatbots to implement safeguards for users, including preventing sexually explicit or suggestive interactions with minors and prohibiting manipulative engagement techniques designed to foster emotional dependence. Users expressing suicidal ideation must be referred to a crisis hotline; public disclosure of crisis referral notification counts required. Defines AI companion chatbot as providing 'adaptive, human-like responses' and sustaining an 'ongoing relationship' across multiple interactions. Excludes business operations, customer service, gaming chat, non-relationship-forming voice assistants, and narrowly tailored educational tools. Passed both chambers.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers

bills.title: KCDPA Amendment Adding Smart TV Automatic Content Recognition Data as Sensitive Data
bills.summary: Would amend the Kentucky Consumer Data Protection Act (KCDPA) to add 'automatic content recognition data' — data captured by a smart television or smart monitor — as a category of sensitive data. Reported favorably from the Committee on Small Business & Information Technology on March 11.
bills.status_detail: Reported favorably from Committee on Small Business & Information Technology on March 11, 2026

bills.title: Maine Comprehensive Consumer Privacy Act
bills.summary: A Maryland-style comprehensive privacy bill that includes substantive data minimization requirements and a prohibition on selling sensitive data. The Senate engrossed LD 1822. Requires a concurrence vote as the House and Senate floor amendments do not match. Maine is close to enacting a comprehensive privacy bill.
bills.status_detail: Senate engrossed; requires concurrence vote as House and Senate floor amendments do not match

bills.title: Nebraska Age-Appropriate Design Code Act Amendment
bills.summary: Passed out of committee and placed on general file with an amendment on March 11. The proposed amendment would change the Act's scope to provide a new exemption for GLBA-regulated entities and cover an online service that 'generates a majority of its annual revenue from online services.'
bills.status_detail: Passed committee; placed on general file with amendment on March 11, 2026; amendment adds GLBA exemption and revenue-based scope test

bills.title: Direct-to-Consumer Genetic Testing Privacy Law
bills.summary: South Dakota is poised to become the latest state to enact a direct-to-consumer genetic testing privacy law after the legislature passed SB 49. Would regulate direct-to-consumer genetic testing, including consumer data rights, consent requirements, and data security obligations. Not yet sent to the governor.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; not yet sent to Governor

bills.title: Utah Consumer Privacy Act Amendment for Motor Vehicle Data Collection
bills.summary: Utah legislature passed an amendment to the Utah Consumer Privacy Act (UCPA). Would apply UCPA to motor vehicle manufacturers that sell or lease vehicles in Utah and collect, transmit, or store personal data through a vehicle data collection system. Would require motor vehicle manufacturers to implement certain in-vehicle privacy controls. Not yet sent to governor.
bills.status_detail: Passed both chambers; not yet sent to Governor
